claim.pdf_says: 1.3.6 Sharing Data ... 1.3.7 Sharing Files ... 1.3.8 Scope of Names
claim.markdown_says: ### 1.3.6 Sharing Data ... ### ║1.3.7 Sharing Files║ ... ### 1.3.8 Scope of Names
claim.why_it_matters: Subsections of 1.3 rendered at the same level as 1.3 (###), inconsistent with 1.3.1/1.3.2 (####); the outline nests them wrongly.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page X-4 (PDF p518) shows the three subsection headings 1.3.6 Sharing Data, 1.3.7 Sharing Files (inside a level-2 box) and 1.3.8 Scope of Names, all subordinate to 1.3 LANGUAGE CONCEPTS. The transcription carries all three headings and all body text (the box markers on 1.3.7 and items (1)-(2) of 1.3.6 match the printed boxes), so nothing is missing. But in specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md the IPC module's '### 1.3 LANGUAGE CONCEPTS' is followed by '#### 1.3.1 Nested Source Programs' and '#### 1.3.2 File Connector', then '### 1.3.3' through '### 1.3.8' (pages 516-518): 1.3.6, 1.3.7 and 1.3.8 sit at the same level as their parent 1.3, so the document outline makes them siblings of 1.3 instead of children. That is a genuine structural defect in the transcription, not page furniture or reflow; it does not change normative text.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a missing heading: the headings 1.3.6, 1.3.7 and 1.3.8 and their text are all present. Their markdown level is wrong: they are '###', the same level as the parent '### 1.3 LANGUAGE CONCEPTS', where the siblings 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 are '####'. The same mis-level affects 1.3.3-1.3.5 on pages 516-517. Fix: demote 1.3.3-1.3.8 of the Inter-Program Communication module to '####'.
